How paid cost and outside interest are calculated

Enter the total you actually pay across all 20 months. The starting example uses ₹40,00,000 total paid and a ₹27,30,000 month-one payout. Interest / cost paid = total paid − payout received = ₹12,70,000. This is the cash cost of the chit, not an annual interest rate. If the payout exceeds total paid, cost is shown as zero and the surplus remains in net gain.

Outside lending rate is annual: 12% means 1% per month. With a month-one payout, the model counts 19 full months after payout until month 20. Outside interest = payout × annual rate ÷ 12 × remaining months ÷ 100. For ₹27,30,000 at 12%, monthly interest is ₹27,300 and interest over 19 months is ₹5,18,700. Principal plus outside interest is ₹32,48,700. Net gain / loss = this amount − ₹40,00,000 = −₹7,51,300.

The full payout is assumed to stay lent out, interest does not compound, and principal is returned at the end. Chit installments are paid separately. The estimate excludes missed repayments and taxes. Month 20 earns no outside interest within this 20-month comparison.

Months 1–19: payout = face value − bid, with commission included in the bid. Month 20: payout = face value − bid − organizer commission. Commission is a percentage of face value and is not subtracted twice. Change bids and total paid to match your scheme; no dividend deductions are assumed beyond the total paid you enter.

Changing face value scales your current bids and total paid proportionally. All values remain editable. Net % = net gain / loss ÷ payout × 100. Monthly net % = Net % ÷ 20; annual net % = monthly net % × 12. These are simple comparison figures, not IRR. Rank 1 has the highest unrounded Net %; it can still represent a loss.

How these estimates work

EMI uses a fixed annual rate, monthly reducing-balance interest and month-end payments. Extra payments start in month one and shorten the term. Fees, taxes and penalties are excluded unless explicitly entered. Flat interest uses the original principal throughout. Loan comparison measures total cash paid, not APR or present value.

Chit figures cover one auction. Organizer commission is included in the auction discount; the remaining discount is shared equally among all members, including the winner. Members equal installments. Actual scheme rules can differ, and future discounts are unknown.
